scope: Shared pages, editorial article fallbacks, commercial helpers, and dedicated legal heroes. Stock subjects are illustrative; no image claims to show Ontiver customers, staff or product interfaces.

contexts: LegalPage /cookies hero: Cookie Policy
entries.reason: The actual policy covers necessary sign-in cookies, device trust and browser storage, with no advertising or cross-site profiling. Searches returned food-cookie photos, premium illustrations and unrelated branded consent screens; none faithfully represents this policy. Use an original browser-and-storage illustration distinguishing session data and saved preferences, informed by MDN and the existing legalDocuments.ts, rather than another generic phone portrait.
entries.creator: Ontiver original diagram
entries.alt: Illustration of a browser connected to necessary session storage and saved preferences

contexts: /security #your-controls: Know the request, choose the claims, review access
entries.reason: The section asks individuals to understand a request and review the information before allowing access. A person actively reading and pointing to a document makes that deliberate review visible, replacing the rejected anonymous phone-and-laptop crop. The original source describes document review at home; the image is illustrative, not an Ontiver permission screen. The 4:3 crop was checked with the reader's face, finger and document retained.

contexts: Fallback article: Why Identity Verification Should Be Reusable
Article cards, related articles and individual blog navigation
entries.reason: The article opens with repeated document uploads and duplicated checks. The paper-heavy administrative scene illustrates that repeated-work problem, rather than suggesting a generic phone use is proof reuse. Models are not depicted as Ontiver users.
entries.creator: cottonbro studio
entries.alt: Three colleagues working through stacks of paper files in an office

contexts: Fallback article: Cutting KYC Costs Without Cutting Assurance

contexts: Fallback article: AML Screening for Product Teams
entries.reason: The article's Give reviewers context section calls for a reviewer to compare source information before dismissing or escalating a possible match. A focused professional sorting and checking several records beside her laptop depicts that active review work, replacing the rejected magnifying-glass still life. The source verifies office document review; the person is an illustrative reviewer, never presented as an AML suspect or an Ontiver employee. The wide article crop retains her face, hands, records and laptop.
entries.creator: Tima Miroshnichenko
entries.alt: A professional reviewing several documents at a desk beside an open laptop

contexts: Fallback article: Building Consent Into Identity Flows
entries.reason: The visible act is inspecting information before deciding, matching clear purpose, scope and meaningful choices. A generic signature-only or checkbox image would misrepresent ongoing request-level consent.
entries.creator: RDNE Stock project
entries.alt: Hands carefully reading through a document in a folder

contexts: Fallback article: A Developer Guide to Verification Webhooks
External developer documentation navigation preview
entries.reason: Actual source code and debugging tools match the article's event processing, duplicate prevention and failure-path debugging. The code is illustrative and is not claimed to implement Ontiver webhooks.
entries.creator: Daniil Komov

contexts: Fallback article: Risk Signals That Matter in Onboarding
entries.reason: The article asks reviewers to connect a signal to evidence, reconcile discrepancies between records and select a justified next action. Two colleagues looking across several documents gives that comparison and human judgement a visible subject, replacing the rejected bank-statement magnifier. The source describes professionals reviewing documents; neither person is depicted as a risky applicant. This collaborative review scene is distinct from the solo reviewer selected for the AML article, and its wide crop preserves both reviewers and the records.
entries.creator: Mikhail Nilov
entries.alt: Two colleagues comparing documents together at a conference table

entries.alt: Hands holding a report with tables and charts for review

contexts: LegalPage /privacy hero: Privacy Policy
entries.reason: A closed combination lock on a computer keyboard clearly illustrates restricted access to personal information. This symbolic still life fits the policy's data protection topic without showing a branded application or claiming to show Ontiver infrastructure. The first candidate was rejected after visual inspection because it actually showed a branded phone and a chained novel, suggesting censorship rather than personal-data protection.
entries.creator: Sasun Bughdaryan
entries.alt: A closed combination padlock resting on a computer keyboard

contexts: LegalPage /account-deletion hero: Account Deletion
entries.reason: The clear deletion word directly identifies the requested account-rights action. It avoids a customer portrait that gives no indication of deletion, and does not imply that all retained records disappear instantly.
entries.creator: Miguel Á. Padriñán
entries.alt: White keyboard letters spelling DELETE on a coral background
